reading: wosi : sore(2)yi : pedemoketme(3)qewi : pqrl : yetemdelowi : (4)pestol : sewilowi (5)atmḫe pi(6)siḫr(7)kte : a(8)tomẖo : pisi(9)ẖte : ḫmlo(10)l : yidotedi(11)kte :
notes: Line 1 name: the first sign is a zigzag-topped sign with a long tail and a separate S to its left, read p e (as in pesto, line 4), not a; '3/3' after desoke could be s o or q; the 3 before l(3) read s, the 3 with a short lower-left tail at (3) read m. pqrl: the second sign is /3 with a closed upper loop, read q (could be s o). yetmdelow?i: the w is drawn as a flat-topped 3 (marked sic). (4)pestol: p e s to l. Line 5-7 'atmḫe pisiḫrkte': 3-shaped signs in pisi and in the line 9 word could be s, m or ẖ; the line-9 word is p i 3 i 3 te. Line 7/8 'a?(8)tosso': the a (S + 2 with long tail) is hatched and marked sic; '33/' could be s s o or s q. Line 10 'ḫmlol' and line 11 'yidotedikte': the two lambda-like signs read d; the first could be te. Griffith prints a small mark above the 9.
check_notes: Name (names table pedemoketmeqewi, Index C): copy 3s read m (de-m-o, t-m-e), the small flat-topped sign before line 3 read e, and the slashed 3 with the slash before it at line 3 read q (step 1 had s, s, l, m o). Formula A table (ato mẖo : pisiẖte) settles the 3s of lines 8-9: m, ẖ and ẖ. Formula B (at mḫe pisiḫrkte) settles s in pisi. yetemdelowi: the te sign was mis-transliterated as t in step 1; the sic w is w per the type. Formula C: both lambda-like signs are d in the printed type (yidotedikte); the table and prose typing 'yidotenikte' is wrong. pestol kept: Index B prints pesetol with se, but the copy clearly has a closed 3 and Index C prints pestol. The type shows no space in 'at mḫe' differently from the copy; spacing kept as in the copy.

reading: wosi : a(2)soreyi : ten?[.](3)dḫitoqowi : mlosḫi(4)li : yerikelowi : metemnise(5)li : tedḫl?lowi : ḫ?r?(6)p?ḫli : semlo(7)wi : pese(8)toli : semlo(9)lowi : ssorli(10)kdiselowi : ḫm(11)loli : ẖ?lkte atomẖe pi(12)siẖte : atmẖe(13)yiḫrkte (14)dbotelito(15)qowi : mlolowi : yeto(16)str : yerikelowi (17)kdeye?t : tedḫelowi : ḫm(18)loli : ẖ[.]lkte : (19)ḫmloli : iplte :
notes: Line 2: S + 2 with long tail before soreyi read a (asoreyi). Line 2-3: after l, a slash and a hatched n (rising stroke, 3, long tail), then one to two signs' width of hatching (one [.] written). Line 3 'tedḫl?lowi': the sign after ḫ has the small flat-topped l shape, though the same word in line 17 has a clear e (tedḫelowi). Line 5-6: right end of the row is broken: one hatched blob and three dotted strokes ([.] x4), then a hatched sign of which the right part looks like i. Line 8 'pese(8)toli': the first sign is zigzag-topped with a long tail and S separate, read p e (cf. Kar. 100 pesto). Line 12 'a?tom?ẖ?e': the S of a is hatched; to is the ɷ form. Line 12-13 'atm?ẖ?l?': the second 3 and the l are hatched. Line 14 'dbo': the V with hooked arm read b. Line 17 starts with a lone flat-topped 2 with long tail, read k (could be a without its S, or p); after e three strokes (y?) and hatching. Line 18: Griffith prints ? over a narrow hatched place between s and l. Last word 'ip?lte': i is written over the tail of the following zigzag sign (p or k). 3-shaped signs (s, m, ẖ) are not separable by shape in this copy; marked ? where the context does not settle them.
check_notes: Name A1 (ten(?)[.]dḫitoqowi): step-1 'lo' is the te sign, and '3//' after to is q + o. Name B1 metemniseli and C1 mlosḫili settle the 3s in lines 3-5. yerikelowi (Index C, twice): the hatched te-like sign in line 4 is l + o. Lines 5-6: Index A/B print ḫr[p]ḫli; the copy's broken stretch is a blob (ḫ?), three dotted strokes (r?) and a hatched zigzag sign with long tail (p?), so the four [.] and i?[.] of step 1 become ḫ?r?(6)p?. semlowi, semlolowi (sic), ssorli kdiselowi, pesetoli, formula A (ato mẖe pisiẖte), formula B (at mẖe yiḫrkte), formula C a/b/c (ḫmloli : ẖ(?)lkte / ẖ▒(?)lkte / iplte) placed. Name A2 dbotelitoqowi: '3//' read q + o. B2 kdeye(?)t(?): hatched place filled with e?, y settled. C2 yetostr. Formula B table prints yiḫrkete; copy and prose have no e before te: kept. tedḫl?lowi (line 3) has no entry and stays; line 17 has e in the same word.

caption: Kar. 102. Stela, on Pl. 27.
notes: Many signs are drawn in thin outline (faint or traced) and wavy lines mark cracks; those signs carry ?. Two plain vertical strokes (one in line 1 before (2), one in line 2/3 before (3)) are not read as signs (likely edges or cracks). Line 1: the first S is crossed by a crack. Line 1 ḫ? is a bold L-shaped sign (ḫ, or to without its dot). Line 2 q?nimni: '/3' could be q or s o; n i m n i, with each n's tail running under the sign before. Line 3 to? is thin, an L with a dot. The V-over-tail group (lines 3, 6, 8) read b k by analogy with elebkwi/wilebkwi. Dotted stretches counted dot by dot: 4 in line 3-4, 10 in line 4-5, 16 in line 5-6, 10 in line 6-7, 6 at the start of line 8. Row 2 has a wide blank gap between its right part and its left part (mlolowi), with no dots. Line 4-5: the hatched sign between the dotted stretches looks like te. Line 6/7: a? is S (thin) + 2 with long tail.
check_notes: Index A/B/C 'are a[mn]ptowi': the cracked S at the start is the left half of a (Griffith restores the 2), the S + tailed sign after re is a, the two thin signs are m and n (bracketed, ?), the zigzag is p and the L-shaped sign is to. 'soni mnitowi': '/3' is s + o, not q; Index B prints a divider after soni, the copy has none. Name A2 bk[.][.][.][.]qowi: '3//' is q + o; 4 dots agree. Name B2 wilo[.][.][.][.]: the type has 4 dots, the copy 10 before the te-like sign; copy kept. Index B '[.][.][.][.] wilebkwi': the copy has 6 dots before wilebkwi; copy kept. Names table column A (person 1) 'lost' and Index C mẖo (form A, Kar. 100, 102) could not be placed: no formula A survives in the copy.
